name: Okta — Sign-in From an Internal (RFC1918) Address
xql_query:
dataset = okta_sso_raw
| filter eventType = "user.session.start"
| alter outcome_result = arrayindex(regextract(outcome, "\"result\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0),
        ip = arrayindex(regextract(client, "\"ipAddress\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0),
        user_name = arrayindex(regextract(actor, "\"alternateId\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0)
| filter outcome_result = "SUCCESS"
| filter ip contains "192.168." or ip contains "10." or ip contains "172.16." or ip contains "172.17." or ip contains "172.18." or ip contains "172.19." or ip contains "172.2" or ip contains "172.31."
| bin _time span = 1h
| comp count() as logins, values(ip) as ip_list by user_name, _time
| fields user_name, ip_list
description: Okta can only see public addresses, so a sign-in recorded from an RFC1918 source means a misconfigured proxy/IdP chain or a forged client address.
alert_name: Okta — Sign-in From an Internal (RFC1918) Address
alert_description:
What fired: Okta can only see public addresses, so a sign-in recorded from an RFC1918 source means a misconfigured proxy/IdP chain or a forged client address.

Why it matters: the IdP is seeing a non-routable client address: a broken proxy/IdP chain or a forged X-Forwarded-For. Assessed severity: Informational.

Investigate:
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity ($user_name) to related activity in the same window.
  - Check the asset inventory / owner for the device or user involved.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized before escalating.
